questions.question: Thirty persons working 6 hours a day can complete a work in 28 days. How many days will 28 persons take to complete another work which is half times the present work, if they work 9 hours a day?
questions.questionHtml: Thirty persons working 6 hours a day can complete a work in 28 days. How many days will 28 persons take to complete another work which is half times the present work, if they work 9 hours a day?
questions.solution:
Formula:

Total work = Total men working × Total time required 

Total time required = hours per day × total days

Calculation:

Total work = 30 × 6 × 28 = 5040 men-hours

Half work = \( 5040\over2\) = 2520 men-hours 

Days required by 28 men to complete half the work working 9 hours a day = \(2520\over 28× 9\) = 10 days

∴ Total time required is 10 days.

questions.question: Working 7 hours a day, 18 persons can complete a certain work in 32 days. In how many days would 14 persons complete the same work, working 8 hours a day?
questions.questionHtml: Working 7 hours a day, 18 persons can complete a certain work in 32 days. In how many days would 14 persons complete the same work, working 8 hours a day?
questions.solution:
As we know,

M1 × D1 × T1 = M2 × D2 × T2

M = Men, D = Days, T = Time

18 × 32 × 7 = 14 × D2 × 8

D2 = (18 × 32 × 7)/14 × 8

D2 = 36

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B can complete the same work in 10 days. With the help of C, working together they completed the work in 5 days. The number of days in which C alone can complete the work is:
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B can complete the same work in 10 days. With the help of C, working together they completed the work in 5 days. The number of days in which C alone can complete the work is:
questions.solution:
Work rate of A = 1/20, Work rate of B = 1/10, Work rate of A + B + C = 1/5

Work rate of C = 1/5 - 1/20 - 2/20, Work rate of C = 4/20 - 3/20, Work rate

of C = 1/20 ⇒ Time taken by C alone = 1 / (Work rate of C) = 20 days

questions.question: P and Q together can do a work in 12 days. P alone can do the same work in 36 days. In how many days can Q alone complete two-third part of the same work?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q together can do a work in 12 days. P alone can do the same work in 36 days. In how many days can Q alone complete two-third part of the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

P + Q = 12 days

P = 36 days

Calculation:

P + Q do a piece of work in =12 days

Work is done by P + Q in 1 day =1/12

P can do the same work in 36 days

Work is done by P in = 1/36

Work is done by both in 1 day = 1/36 +1/12 

The efficiency of P and Q is 2 and 1 (3 – 1)

Q alone complete two-third part of the same work = 36 × 2/3 = 24

Q complete the work of = 24/2 = 12 days 

Hence Q complete the work in = 12 days

questions.question: A is 40% more efficient than B. How much time will both, working together, take to finish the work, which B alone can finish in 36 days?
questions.questionHtml: A is 40% more efficient than B. How much time will both, working together, take to finish the work, which B alone can finish in 36 days?
questions.solution:
A is 40% more efficient than B, then the efficiency of A : B = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5

B alone can finish in 36 days, then total work = (5 × 36) = 180 unit

If A & B both working together, time taken = 180/(7 + 5) = 180/12 = 15 days

questions.solution:

Total work = 20 × 2 = 40 units

Time taken to complete the work = 40/5 = 8 days

questions.question: On a construction site, Pankaj and Tarun are two workers who have been assigned to break the stones for flooring. Pankaj can complete the work alone in 16 h, while Tarun will take 24 h. They decided to work on the alternate hours so that they can take rest in between. Pankaj starts in the first hour and then Tarun and so on. In how many hours will they complete the work together if they work on the basis of alternate hours?
questions.questionHtml: On a construction site, Pankaj and Tarun are two workers who have been assigned to break the stones for flooring. Pankaj can complete the work alone in 16 h, while Tarun will take 24 h. They decided to work on the alternate hours so that they can take rest in between. Pankaj starts in the first hour and then Tarun and so on. In how many hours will they complete the work together if they work on the basis of alternate hours?
questions.solution:
Given:- Pankaj can complete the work in 16 hours, and Traun can complete the work in 24 hours

To find:- In how many hours will they complete the work together if they work on the basis of alternate hours

Formula used:- Work done = efficiency × time taken

Calculation:- 

Pankaj can complete the work in 16 hours

Traun can complete the work in 24 hours

Alternate hours starting from Pankaj,

Let the total work be LCM (16, 24),

⇒Total work = 48 unit

Efficiency of Pankaj = \(\frac{total\ work}{time\ taken\ alone}\) = \(\frac{48}{16}\)

⇒Efficiency of Pankaj = 3 unit/ h

Similarly, Efficiency of Tarun = 2 unit/ h

⇒ Pankaj will do 3 units of work in 1 hour and in next hour 2 units will be done by Tarun, which means in 2 hours they're doing 5 units of work

⇒In 2 hours 5 unit of work will be completed,

⇒Time taken to complete 45 unit of work = \(\frac{45}{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)} = 18 hours \)

Therefore, the left work now = 48 - 45 = 3 units

⇒The 3 units will be don't by Pankaj in the 19th hour.

 

.·.In 19 hours will they complete the work together if they work on the basis of alternate hours

questions.question: Ten men or twelve women can finish the same work in 10 days. If 5 men and 2 women undertake the work together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: Ten men or twelve women can finish the same work in 10 days. If 5 men and 2 women undertake the work together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let efficiency of 1 man and 1 woman be m and w respectively.

10m = 12w

⇒ m : w = 6 : 5

Total work = 10 × 6 × 10 = 600 units

Work done by 5 men and 2 women in 1 day = 5 × 6 + 2 × 5 = 40

∴ Number of days = 600/40 = 15 days

questions.question: 30 men working 8 hours per day can dig a pond in 16 days. By working how many hours per day can 32 men dig the same pond in 20 days?
questions.questionHtml: 30 men working 8 hours per day can dig a pond in 16 days. By working how many hours per day can 32 men dig the same pond in 20 days?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

M1 = 30 men, T1 = 8 hrs, D1 = 16 days, M2 = 32 men, D2 = 20 days

According to the formula

30 × 8 × 16 = 32 × T2 × 20

⇒ T2 = (30 × 8 × 16)/(32 × 20)

∴ T2 = 6 hrs.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 9 days and 15 days, respectively. If they work together, then the work will be completed in:
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a piece of work in 9 days and 15 days, respectively. If they work together, then the work will be completed in:

Combined rate = 1/9 + 1/15 = 8/45

Time to complete = 1 / (8/45) = 45/8 = \(5 \frac{5}{8}\) days

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days. B and C can do the same work in 60 days. A and C can do the same work in 45 days. In how many days can B alone complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days. B and C can do the same work in 60 days. A and C can do the same work in 45 days. In how many days can B alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B can do a piece of work in 36 days,

B and C can do the same work in 60 days,

A and C can do the same work in 45 days.

Concept used:

Efficiency = 1/(Total time)

Calculation:

(A + B)’s 1 day work = 1/36      ----(i) 

(B + C)’s 1 day work = 1/60      ----(ii) 

(C + A)’s 1 day work = 1/45      ----(iii)

From equations (i), (ii) and (iii),

2(A + B + C)’s 1 day work = 1/36 + 1/60 + 1/45

⇒ (5 + 3 + 4)/180 = 1/15

⇒ (A + B + C)’s 1 day work = 1/(15 × 2) = 1/30      ----(iv)

From equations (iii) and (iv) we get

B’s 1 day work = 1/30 – 1/45 = (3 – 2)/90 = 1/90

Time taken by B alone to complete the work = 90

∴ B alone can complete the same work in 90 days

 Alternate Method

Let us find the LCM of  36, 60 and 45

LCM of 36, 60 and 45 = 180

Let the total work be 180 units. 

A + B can do = 180/36 = 5 units/day      ----(i)

B + C can do = 180/60 = 3 units/day      ----(ii)

C + A can do = 180/45 = 4 units/day      ----(iii) 

Adding the above equations, we get 

2(A + B + C) = 5 + 3 + 4 

⇒ A + B + C = 12/2 = 6      ----(iv)

Subtracting equation (iii) from (iv) 

B = 6 - 4 = 2units/day 

⇒ Time taken by B = 180/2 = 90days

∴ B alone can complete the same work in 90 days

questions.question: A and B can finish a work in 10 days, B and C can finish it in 12 days and C and A can finish in 6 days. In how many days A alone can finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can finish a work in 10 days, B and C can finish it in 12 days and C and A can finish in 6 days. In how many days A alone can finish the work?
questions.solution:
Let total work is 60 units ( LCM of 6, 10 , and12 and)

The efficiency of A+B  = 60 /10 ⇒ 6 units

The efficiency of B+C = 60 / 12⇒ 5 units

The efficiency of A+C = 60 / 6⇒ 10 units

Total efficiency of A + B + C is (10 + 5 + 6) / 2 = 21/2

The efficiency of A is 21 / 2 - 5 = 11/2 units

The number of days A required is 60 × 2 / 11 = 120 /11 days

questions.question: Sarthak and Mohan are working on alternate days in a workshop. Sarthak can complete the work in 20 days while Mohan can finish in 25 days. Sarthak works on the 1st day, Mohan on the 2nd day, and so on. How much time (in days) will they take on alternate basis?
questions.questionHtml: Sarthak and Mohan are working on alternate days in a workshop. Sarthak can complete the work in 20 days while Mohan can finish in 25 days. Sarthak works on the 1st day, Mohan on the 2nd day, and so on. How much time (in days) will they take on alternate basis?
questions.solution:
Given:

Sarthak can complete the work in 20 days

Mohan can complete the work in 25 days

Sarthak works on the 1st day, Mohan on the 2nd day, and so on.

Formula used:

Work done by Sarthak in 1 day = 1/20

Work done by Mohan in 1 day = 1/25

Combined work in 2 days = Work done by Sarthak in 1 day + Work done by Mohan in 1 day

Calculation:

Combined work in 2 days = (1/20) + (1/25)

⇒ Combined work in 2 days = (5 + 4) / 100

⇒ Combined work in 2 days = 9/100

Total work = 1

Number of such 2 day cycles required to complete the work:

⇒ Total work / Combined work in 2 days

⇒ 1 / (9/100)

⇒ 100/9 ≈ 11 cycles

Work done in 11 cycles or 22 days = 11 × 9/100 = 99/100

Remaining work = 1 - 99/100 = 1/100

Now, Sarthak complete this work in 20/100 = 1/5.

Total days = 22 1/5.

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: A is twice as good a workman as B and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days. In how many days will B alone finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: A is twice as good a workman as B and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days. In how many days will B alone finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A is twice as good a workman as B and together they finish a piece of work in 13 days.

Concept Used:

Efficiency ∝ 1/Time

Calculation:

The efficiency ratio of A and B is 2 : 1

The time ratio of A and B is 1 : 2

Let, A took time x days and B took time 2x days to complete the work alone

In 1 day A can do 1/x part of the work

In 1 day B can do 1/2x part of the work

Together in 1 day they can do 1/13 part of the work

(1/x) + (1/2x) = 1/13

⇒ 3/2x = 1/13

⇒ x = 39/2

B alone will finish the work in 2 × (39/2)

= 39 days

∴ In 39 days B alone will finish the work.

questions.question: 10 men or 15 women can complete a work in 30 days. In how many days can 15 men and 27 women complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: 10 men or 15 women can complete a work in 30 days. In how many days can 15 men and 27 women complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

10 men or 15 women can complete a work in 30 days

Calculation:

Let the new time be x days

10M × 30 = 15W × 30

⇒ 300M = 450W

⇒ 2M = 3W

Total work = 10 × 30 = 300 units

Now 15M and 27W = 15M and 18M [Converted women into men]

So, time = 300/33 = 100/11 days or \(9\frac{1}{11}\)days

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 15 days. If A, B and C working together can complete the same work in 10 days, then in how many days can C alone complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can complete a work in 15 days. If A, B and C working together can complete the same work in 10 days, then in how many days can C alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken by A and B to complete the work = 15 days

Time taken by A, B and C to complete the work = 10 days

Calculation:

Work done by A and B in one day = \(1\over15\) 

Work done by A, B and C in one day = \(1\over10\)

Work done by C in one day = \(1\over10\) - \(1\over15\) = \(1\over30\)

∴ Time taken by C to complete the work = 30 days

C can complete the work in 30 days.

Alternate MethodLCM of 10 and 15 = 30

Let the total work be 30 units

Efficiency of A and B = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units 

Efficiency of A, B and C = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units

Efficiency of C = 3 - 2 = 1 unit

Time taken by C = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days and 25 days, respectively. They work on alternate days,starting with A till the work gets completed. How long (in days) would it take A and B to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days and 25 days, respectively. They work on alternate days,starting with A till the work gets completed. How long (in days) would it take A and B to complete the work?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

A can do a piece of work in 20 days

B can do a piece of work in 25 days 

FORMULA USED:

Efficiency = Total work/No. of days

CALCULATION:

Let us assume total work be ( L.C.M of 20,25) be100 unit 

( you can assume any number but for the sake of calculation it is advised to take L.C.M. of the given numbers)

Efficiency of A  = work done by A in 1 day = 100/20 = 5 

Efficiency of B = work done by B in 1 day = 100/25 = 4 

Now, work done in 2 days = 9 

So, in 10 pair of 2 days they will complete 9 × 10 = 90 unit of work 

In 20 days 90 unit of work is done 

Remaining work = (100 - 90 ) = 10 unit 

As, they work alternately with A as first .So, on 21st day another 5 unit of work will be done 

Now, remaining 5 unit of work has to be done by B on 22nd day since its efficiency is 4 . 4/5 work is done 

Now ( 1- 4/5)= 1/5 work is done by A on 23rd day 

So, No. of days taken to complete the whole work = complete 22 days + 1/5 of 23rd day = ( 22 + 1/5)

Hence, A and B together takes 22 1/5  days to complete the work.

9 (R + S) 44/9

Total time taken by P, Q, R, and S together to complete the work ⇒ 44/19 = 2\(6\over19\) days

questions.question: In a factory, Ajay and Vijay work on the same machine to cut diamonds but on alternate hour basis. Ajay works for the first hour and then Vijay works for the second hour and so on. Ajay can complete the work in 6 hours, while Vijay completes it in 16 hours if they work individually. In how much time can they complete the work if they are using the machine on alternate basis?
questions.questionHtml: In a factory, Ajay and Vijay work on the same machine to cut diamonds but on alternate hour basis. Ajay works for the first hour and then Vijay works for the second hour and so on. Ajay can complete the work in 6 hours, while Vijay completes it in 16 hours if they work individually. In how much time can they complete the work if they are using the machine on alternate basis?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM (6,16) = 48, so efficiency of Ajay = 48/6 = 8 and efficiency of Vijay = 3

As they work in alternative basis, In 2 hours = 8 + 3 = 11 work is done ⇒ in 8 hours = 44 work

The remaining 44 work has to be done by Ajay in 4/8 = 0.5 hours = 30 minutes 

Total time taken by Ajay and Vjay to complete the work on alternative basis = 8h + 30min

questions.question: A can complete a certain work in 30 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 20% more efficient than B. They all worked together for 3 days. B alone will complete the remaining work in:
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a certain work in 30 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 20% more efficient than B. They all worked together for 3 days. B alone will complete the remaining work in:
questions.solution:
Let Efficiency of A = 4

Efficiency of B = 4 × 5/4 = 5

Efficiency of C = 5 × 6/5 = 6

Total work = 30 × 4 = 120

Work done by A, B and C in 3 days = (4 + 5 + 6) × 3 = 45

Remaining work = 120 – 45 = 75

∴ B completes the remaining work in = 75/5 = 15 days

questions.question: A and B can finish a work together in 30 days. B and C can finish the same work together in 24 days. A and C can finish the work together in 40 days. If all three work together, how long will it take them to complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can finish a work together in 30 days. B and C can finish the same work together in 24 days. A and C can finish the work together in 40 days. If all three work together, how long will it take them to complete the work?
questions.solution:
Efficiency of (A + B) (B + C) and (C + A) together = A + B + B + C + C + A = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12

2(A + B + C) = 12

A + B + C = 6

Time taken by (A + B + C) to complete the work = 120/6 = 20 days

Alternate Solution∶

Efficiency of A and B when they work together = 1/30

Efficiency of B and C when they work together = 1/24

Efficiency of A and C when they work together = 1/40

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B), (B + C) and (C + A) when they work together = 1/30 + 1/24 + 1/40

= (4 + 5 + 3)/120 = 12/120 = 1/10

∴ Efficiency of A, B and C when they work together = 1/2 × 1/10 = 1/20

Time taken by A, B and C to complete the work when they work together

= 1/(1/20) = 20 days.

questions.question: Ram and Ramesh can do a work in 12 days, Ramesh and Somesh in 15 days and Somesh and Ram in 10 days. If Ram, Ramesh and Somesh work together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: Ram and Ramesh can do a work in 12 days, Ramesh and Somesh in 15 days and Somesh and Ram in 10 days. If Ram, Ramesh and Somesh work together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ram and Ramesh can do work together =12 days

Ramesh and Somesh can do work together = 15 days

Somesh and Ram can do work together = 10 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

Let the Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh can complete the work together in X days

One day work of Ramesh and Ram =  \({1\over12}\)

One day work of Ramesh and Somesh = \({1\over15}\)

One day work of Somesh and Ram = \({1\over10}\)

One day work of all three = \({1\over12}+{1\over15}+{1\over10}\) = \({5+4+6\over60}={15\over60}={1\over4}\)

Working twice they can complete the work in = 4 days

They can complete the work = 8 days

∴ The required result will be 8 days.

Alternate MethodCalculation:

Ram and Ramesh = 12 days

Ramesh and Somesh = 15 days

Somesh and Ram = 10 days 

LCM of (12,15, & 10)  = 60 units

Efficiency of Ram and Ramesh = 60/12 = 5 units

Efficiency of Ramesh and Somesh = 60/15 = 4 units

Efficiency of Somesh and Ram = 60/10 = 6 units

Efficiency of 2(Ram, Ramesh & Somesh) = 15 units(5 + 4 + 6)

Total Efficiency of  Ram, Ramesh & Somesh = (5 + 4 + 6)/2 = 7.5 units

Time taken by Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh together to complete the work:

Time = Total work / Total Efficiency

⇒ 60/7.5 = 8 days 

∴ Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh together will complete the work in 8 days.

questions.question: A man, a woman and a boy can complete a work in 3, 4 and 12 days, respectively. How many boys must assist one man and one woman to complete the same work in one day?
questions.questionHtml: A man, a woman and a boy can complete a work in 3, 4 and 12 days, respectively. How many boys must assist one man and one woman to complete the same work in one day?
questions.solution:
Man's 1 day work = 1/3, Woman's 1 day work = 1/4

Boy's 1 day work = 1/12

⇒ 1 × (1/3) + 1 × (1/4) + x × (1/12) = 1 { ∵ x be the no. of boys needed} 

⇒ x/12 = 1 - (1/3) - (1/4) ⇒ x/12 = (12 - 7)/12 ⇒ x = 5

questions.question: A and B working together can do 45% of the work in 9 days. A alone can do the work in 30 days. How many days will B alone take to do the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B working together can do 45% of the work in 9 days. A alone can do the work in 30 days. How many days will B alone take to do the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A = 30 days

A + B = 45% of work in 9 days

Calculation:

A + B = 45% of work in 9 days

A + B = 100% of work will be completed in (9/45) × 100 = 20 days

So, (A + B) together can complete the work in 20 days

A alone can do the work in 30 days.

Suppose the total work is 60 units.

A’s one day work = 60/30 = 2 units

(A+ B)’s one day work = 60/20 = 3 units

∴ B’s one day work = (3 – 2) = 1 unit

So, B alone can do the work in 60/1 = 60 days

questions.question: Raju and Ramu together can do a piece of work in 8 days, and Raju alone can do it in 12 days. In how many days can Ramu alone do it?
questions.questionHtml: Raju and Ramu together can do a piece of work in 8 days, and Raju alone can do it in 12 days. In how many days can Ramu alone do it?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Raju and Ramu together can do a piece of work = 8 days

Raju alone can do it = 12 days

CALCULATION:

(Raju + Ramu) → 8

Raju → 12

The LCM of 8 and 12 is 24 (24 is the total work)

⇒Work efficiency of Raju and Ramu = 24/8 = 3

⇒Work efficiency of Raju = 24/12 =2

⇒The work efficiency of Ramu = 3-2 = 1

Now, Ramu can alone do it = 24/1 = 24 days.

Option 4 is the correct.

questions.question: The efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 5 : 6 : 8 working together, they can complete a piece of work in 120 hours. In how many hours will, B alone be able be to complete 40% of that work?
questions.questionHtml: The efficiencies of A, B and C are in the ratio 5 : 6 : 8 working together, they can complete a piece of work in 120 hours. In how many hours will, B alone be able be to complete 40% of that work?

40% of the total work = 2280 × 40/100 = 912

B alone can complete the 40% of the total work = 912/6 = 152 days.

questions.question: Raj can build a house in 16 days by himself, while Suraj can do it in 12 days. Raj and Suraj work on alternate days. How many days would the house take to build if Raj starts working on the first day?
questions.questionHtml: Raj can build a house in 16 days by himself, while Suraj can do it in 12 days. Raj and Suraj work on alternate days. How many days would the house take to build if Raj starts working on the first day?
questions.solution:
Given:

Raj can build a house = in 16 days

Suraj can build a house = in 12 days 

Formula used:

Efficiency = Total unit / No. of days

Calculation:

Let the total unit of work be L.C.M of 16 and 12  48 unit

( you can assume any number but for the sake of calculation, it is advised to take L.C.M of the given numbers) 

Now, Efficiency of Raj = Raj 1 day work = 48/16 = 3 

Also, Efficiency of Suraj = Suraj 1 day work = 48/12 = 4 

⇒ 2 days work of Raj and Suraj =  3 + 4  = 7 

Now in 6 pairs of days, they will do =  7 × 6  unit 

⇒ 12 days of work = 42 unit 

⇒ Remaining work = (48 - 42) = 6 unit 

As Raj works 1st. So, on the 13th day, 3 more units of work will be done by him 

Now, only ( 6 - 3 ) = 3 unit work is to be done, which will be done by Suraj, as they work alternatively 

⇒ 14th day work = 3/4  work is done . So, it takes 13 3/4 days to complete the whole work 

Hence, the house would take 13 3/4 days to be built.

Shortcut Trick                 Time        Work        Efficiency

⇒ Raju =   16           48               3

⇒ Suraj =  12          48               4

⇒  Days      1st         2nd

                   Raju      Suraj

⇒ Work      3 unit       4 unit  

⇒ 2 days = 7 unit work

⇒ 12 days = 42 units of work

⇒ 13 days = 45 units of work

⇒ 14th day Suraj will perform = 3/4 day

⇒ complete work will be completed in 13(3/4) days.

questions.question: Anil and Bipin together can complete a work in 15 days, while Bipin alone can finish It 20 days. In how many days can Anil alone finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: Anil and Bipin together can complete a work in 15 days, while Bipin alone can finish It 20 days. In how many days can Anil alone finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given : 

Anil and Bipin together can complete a work in 15 days.

Bipin alone can finish it in 20 days.

Formula Used : 

Work done = time × efficiency

Calculation : 

Total work = LCM (15, 20) = 60

Efficiency of Anil and Bipin = 4

Efficiency of Bipin = 3 

Efficiency of Anil = 4 - 3 = 1 

Time taken by Anil = 60/1 = 60 days

∴ The correct answer is 60 days.

questions.question: A certain number of persons can complete a work in 54 days. If there were 15 persons less, it would take 18 days more for the work to be completed. Initially, the number persons is:
questions.questionHtml: A certain number of persons can complete a work in 54 days. If there were 15 persons less, it would take 18 days more for the work to be completed. Initially, the number persons is:
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodLet the number men be x.

Number of days in the second case = 54 + 18 = 72

54 × x = 72 × (x - 15)

⇒ 54x = 72x - 1080

⇒ 18x = 1080

⇒ x = 60

Traditional method:

Given:

Certain people can complete work in = 54 days.

Calculation:

Let certain number of people be N.

N people's 1 day's work = 1/54

1 people 1 day's work = 1/54N

For (N - 15) people = work will be completed in 72 days

(N - 15) people's 1 day's work = 1/72

For this case, 1 people 1 day's work = 1/[72(N - 15)]

Then,

⇒ 1/54N = 1/[72(N - 15)]

⇒ 72N - 1080 = 54N

⇒ N = 60

∴ Initially, there are 60 persons.

questions.question: P and Q can finish a work in 10 days and 5 days, respectively. Q worked for 2 days and left the job. In how many days can P alone finish the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q can finish a work in 10 days and 5 days, respectively. Q worked for 2 days and left the job. In how many days can P alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Given:

P can complete a work = 10 days

Q can complete a work = 5 days

Q worked for 2 days and remaining work finished by P

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Work/Time

Concept Used:

Total Work is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of time taken by all the persons individually.

Calculation:

Let the remaining work can be finished by P in T days 

Total Work = LCM of 10, 5 

⇒ Total Work = 10 

Efficiency of P = 10/10 = 1

Efficiency of Q = 10/5 = 2 

Total Work = Work done by P + Work done by Q

⇒ 10 = 1 × T + 2 × 2 = T + 4

⇒ T = 10 – 4 = 6 Days

⇒ T = 6 Days

∴ In 6 days P alone can finish the remaining work

Alternate Method

LCM of 10 and 5 = 10 units= Total work

Efficiency of P = 10/10 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of Q = 10/5 = 2 units/day

Now, Q alone worked for 2 days which means that work done by Q in 2 days = (2 × 2) = 4 units

Now, work left = (10 – 4) = 6 units

Time taken by P to complete remaining work = 6/1 = 6 days

∴ In 6 days P alone can finish the remaining work

questions.question: Nirmal completed the school project in 45 days. How many days will Amit take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Nirmal?
questions.questionHtml: Nirmal completed the school project in 45 days. How many days will Amit take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Nirmal?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken by Nirmal to complete the project = 45 days

Amit is 25% more efficient than Nirmal

Formula Used:

Efficiency and Time are inversely proportional.

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of Nirmal be 100 units.

Then, efficiency of Amit = 100 + 25 = 125 units

Since Efficiency ∝ 1/Time, we have:

Time taken by Amit = (Efficiency of Nirmal / Efficiency of Amit) × Time taken by Nirmal

⇒ Time taken by Amit = (100 / 125) × 45

⇒ Time taken by Amit = (4 / 5) × 45

⇒ Time taken by Amit = 36 days

Amit will take 36 days to complete the same work.

questions.question: If 10 men can complete a piece of work in 12 days by working 7 hours a day, then in how many days can 14 men do the same work by working 6 hours a day?
questions.questionHtml: If 10 men can complete a piece of work in 12 days by working 7 hours a day, then in how many days can 14 men do the same work by working 6 hours a day?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Total work = M × H × D

M = Number of person, H = Number of the hour, D = Number of days,

Let the number of days be d, then

According to the question

10 × 12 × 7 = 14 × d × 6

D = (10 × 12 × 7)/(14 × 6)

D = 10 days

questions.question: Ramu works 4 times as fast as Somu. If Somu can complete a work in 20 days independently, then the number of days in which Ramu and Somu together can complete the work is:
questions.questionHtml: Ramu works 4 times as fast as Somu. If Somu can complete a work in 20 days independently, then the number of days in which Ramu and Somu together can complete the work is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio of Ramu to Somu = 4 : 1

Total Work = Somu's Efficiency × Somu's Time = 1 × 20 = 20 units

Combined Efficiency = 4 + 1 = 5 units

Time taken together = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 days

∴ The correct answer is 4 days.

Alternate Method

Given: Ramu is 4 times faster than Somu. Somu takes 20 days.

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Somu 20 20 20 ÷ 20 = 1
Ramu 20 ÷ 4 = 5 20 ÷ 5 = 4

⇒ Somu's efficiency = 1 unit/day

⇒ Ramu's efficiency = 4 × 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Total Work = 1 × 20 = 20 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of Ramu and Somu = 4 + 1 = 5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by both = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 days

∴ The correct answer is 4 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If the ratio of efficiencies of A and B is x : y, then the ratio of time taken is y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a work in x days and B can do it in y days, then they together can do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the efficiency or the actual work done by the workers.

questions.question: Sara can finish a work in 18 days and Tara can complete the same work in 15 days. Tara worked for 10 days and left the job. In how many days can Sara finish the remaining work alone?
questions.questionHtml: Sara can finish a work in 18 days and Tara can complete the same work in 15 days. Tara worked for 10 days and left the job. In how many days can Sara finish the remaining work alone?

∴ The required result will be 6 days.

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 50 days. If A is 40% less efficient than B, in how many days can A working alone complete 60% of the work?

questions.question: A completes a piece of work in 4 days and B completes it in 6 days. How long will it take to complete the same piece of work if they both work together?
questions.questionHtml: A completes a piece of work in 4 days and B completes it in 6 days. How long will it take to complete the same piece of work if they both work together?
questions.solution:
Given:

A's time to complete the work alone = 4 days.

B's time to complete the work alone = 6 days.

Formula Used:

Combined work rate = 1 / (1/A's time + 1/B's time)

Calculation:

Work rate of A = 1/4

Work rate of B = 1/6

Combined work rate = 1/4 + 1/6

Combined work rate = (1)/(4) + (1)/(6)

⇒ Combined work rate = (3)/(12) + (2)/(12)

⇒ Combined work rate = (5)/(12)

Time taken to complete the work together = 1 / Combined work rate

Time taken to complete the work together = (12)/(5) days

Time taken to complete the work together = 2 2/5 days

The time taken to complete the work if A and B work together is 2 2/5 days.

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively. They completed the work in 9 days with the help of C. How many days will C take to complete eight-ninths of the work alone?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively. They completed the work in 9 days with the help of C. How many days will C take to complete eight-ninths of the work alone?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively.

They completed the work in 9 days with the help of C. 

Concept used:

Work = efficiency × time

Calculation:

Total work = LCM [27, 54] = 54

∴ Efficiency of A = 54/27 = 2 units/day 

Efficiency of B = 54/54 = 1 unit/day 

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 54/9 = 6 units/day

Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) - {Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B}

Efficiency of C = (6 - {2 + 1}) = 3 units/day

Time taken by C to complete eight-ninths of the work alone = 8/9 × 54/3 = 16 days

∴ The correct answer is 16 days.

⇒ \({5\over24}={1\over X}\)

∴ They can complete the work in 4.8 hours.

questions.question: P completes a work in 12 days and Q in 24 days. In how many days P and Q working together can complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->P completes a work in 12 days and Q in 24 days. In how many days P and Q working together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

P completes a work in 12 days and Q in 24 days.

Formula used:

Work rate of P = 1/12 work/day

Work rate of Q = 1/24 work/day

Combined work rate of P and Q = 1/12 + 1/24 work/day

Calculation:

Combined work rate = 1/12 + 1/24

⇒ Combined work rate = 2/24 + 1/24

⇒ Combined work rate = 3/24

⇒ Combined work rate = 1/8 work/day

Time to complete the work together = 1 / (1/8)

⇒ Time to complete the work together = 8 days

∴ The correct answer is option 2.

Alternate Method L.C.M (12,24) = 24 (Total work)

A does = 24/12 = 2 units of work in one day.

B does = 24/24 = 1 unit of work in one day.

Together A and B do = 2+1 = 3 units of work in one day.

So, they finish work in 24 / 3 = 8 days.

questions.question: A can finish a piece of the work in 16 days and B can finish it in 12 days. They worked together for 4 days and then A left. B finished the remaining work. For how many total number of days did B work to finish the work completely?
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a piece of the work in 16 days and B can finish it in 12 days. They worked together for 4 days and then A left. B finished the remaining work. For how many total number of days did B work to finish the work completely?
questions.solution:
A can finish in 1 day = 1/16 work, A can finish in 4 days = 4/16 = 1/4 work,

B can finish in 1 day = 1/12 work, B can finish in 4 days = 4/12 = 1/3 work

The remaining work = 1 - [(1/4) + (1/3)] = 1 - (7/12) = 5/12

Time taken by B to finish the work = (5/12) ÷ (1/12) = (5/12) × 12 = 5 days

Total number of days B work = 4 + 5 = 9 days
